verdict_guidance.correct: Use only when code quality is solid and there is no strong static or execution-based evidence of incorrect behavior.
verdict_guidance.acceptable_with_minor_notes: Use when the solution is basically correct but has low-risk issues, mild style problems, or small improvement opportunities.
verdict_guidance.needs_fix: Use when the main direction is recoverable but there are concrete defects, failed visible cases, missing edge-case handling, or compile/runtime concerns that need correction.
verdict_guidance.incorrect: Use when compile failure, major logic mismatch, severe incompleteness, or strong execution evidence shows the submission does not solve the task.

execution_evidence_priorities: Compile error or explicit execution failure overrides speculative static optimism.
Visible failed cases should be referenced concretely when they explain the defect.
If only pass-count summary exists without visible failures, describe the problem cautiously and avoid inventing exact hidden inputs.
Runtime and memory figures may support efficiency comments but should not be over-interpreted without task constraints.
